activity.notes: Joan of Constantinople inherited Flanders after the death of her father Baldwin IX in 1205 and remained Countess of Flanders until her death on 5 December 1244. Her minority initially required regency and her husbands later shared political authority, but her comital title and dynastic sovereignty were continuous. ATLAS records her as a ruling countess of the County of Flanders rather than merely as a count's consort.

sources.title: Columbia University Epistolae — Joan of Constantinople, Countess of Flanders
sources.citation_text: Columbia's Epistolae project identifies Joan as Countess of Flanders and explains that the death of Baldwin in 1205 left Joan and her sister as heirs, with a regent ruling in Joan's name during her minority.

sources.title: Bibliothèque nationale de France — Jeanne (1200?-1244 ; comtesse de Flandre)
sources.citation_text: The BnF authority record identifies Jeanne/Joan of Constantinople as Countess of Flanders from 1205 to 1244 and records her death on 5 December 1244.
